Colleen Brown Whiting LD 2014
To the Joint Standing Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs,
I am writing as a Maine taxpayer in support of LD 2014, An Act to Update the Funding Method for Career and Technical Education Programs.
Maine has a workforce problem that cannot be solved by sending every student to a four-year college. We need electricians, welders, healthcare workers, mechanics, builders, and technicians. Career and Technical Education programs are the pipeline for those jobs, yet the way we fund them is outdated and does not reflect today's costs, enrollment, or workforce demand.
As a taxpayer, I want my dollars invested where they actually produce results. CTE programs give students practical skills that lead directly to good-paying jobs in Maine. They also keep young people engaged in school who might otherwise drop out or leave the state.
Right now, districts that try to expand or improve their CTE offerings are often penalized by funding formulas that do not keep up with inflation, equipment costs, or the need for modern training facilities. That discourages growth at exactly the time Maine needs more skilled workers.
Updating the funding method will help ensure these programs are stable, accessible, and aligned with real labor market needs. That is a smart use of public money and a smart investment in Maine's future workforce.
LD 2014 supports students, employers, and taxpayers at the same time. I urge the committee to support this bill.
Thank you for considering my testimony.

TESTIMONY IN SUPPORT OF
L.D. 2014
AN ACT TO UPDATE THE FUNDING METHOD FOR CAREER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION PROGRAMS
Senator Rafferty, Representative Murphy, and members of the Education and Cultural Affairs Committee, I am Eric Waddell, Executive Director for Maine School Management Association, testifying on behalf of the legislative committees of the Maine School Boards Association and Maine School Superintendents Association in strong support of L.D. 2014. Our associations represent more than 1,500 school board members and more than 250 superintendents and assistant superintendents, and we advocate on behalf of strong, equitable, and sustainable public education systems across our state.
Interest in Career and Technical Education (CTE) programming among Maine students is growing rapidly. Across the state, students increasingly recognize the relevance and value of a CTE education, not only as preparation for immediate entry into the workforce, but also as a pathway to further postsecondary education, industry credentials, and long-term career success.
Today's students are also more aware than ever of the growing college debt crisis in the United States. They are becoming increasingly savvy about the long-term financial implications of postsecondary choices and are weighing return on investment more carefully than previous generations. As a result, many students see technical education as a high-value option that offers practical skills, meaningful credentials, and strong earning potential without the burden of crushing debt.
The challenge facing Maine's CTE centers, however, is not a lack of student interest--it is capacity. In many regions of the state, there are far more prospective students than there are available seats in CTE programs. This reality limits access to high-quality programming and constrains our ability to respond to workforce needs across Maine's economy.
L.D. 2014 offers a practical and sensible strategy to help address this challenge. By moving from a three-year to a two-year enrollment average for the purposes of calculating funding, this legislation provides a more responsive and realistic reflection of actual student demand.
Importantly, it also helps get funding to CTE centers more quickly, allowing them to plan, staff, and expand programs in a more timely and effective manner.
This change will better align funding with enrollment trends, support program growth, and ultimately allow more Maine students to access the CTE opportunities they are actively seeking.
For these reasons, our local school leaders strongly support L.D. 2014. Thank you for your continued commitment to Maine's students and public education system.

Eric F. Waddell
MSBA Executive Director
